title: Asymmetric borrow on HeaderDateTime conversion helpers: to_mail_parser(self), from_mail_parser(&DateTime)
description: header_typed.rs:97 takes `self` by value (HeaderDateTime is Copy). header_typed.rs:111 takes `&mail_parser::DateTime` by reference. mail_parser::DateTime is itself a Copy type composed entirely of small primitives (u16, u8, bool); taking it by reference forces the caller to dereference and serves no purpose. The asymmetry signals the author did not think about the borrow uniformly. Idiomatic: pick by-value for both (since both types are Copy) or by-reference for both. Take by-value matches the corresponding `From` impl signature (`From<T>`, not `From<&T>`), which is the other change MIME-o2c.[From-trait] suggests.
close_reason: Type-definition cleanup batch on the typed header surface: (.4) added #[non_exhaustive] to EmailAddress and AddressGroup (HeaderDateTime was already done); (.5) dropped Copy from HeaderDateTime; (.26) dropped Copy from HeaderForm; (.18/.19/.20) added Display impls — RFC 5322 §3.4 mailbox/group form for EmailAddress/AddressGroup, RFC 3339 form for HeaderDateTime; (.34/.35) added Hash on EmailAddress/AddressGroup/HeaderDateTime/HeaderValueTyped; (.36) added Default on EmailAddress/AddressGroup; (.33) symmetric by-value internal signature on to_mail_parser/from_mail_parser. New public constructors EmailAddress::new and AddressGroup::new for callers blocked by #[non_exhaustive]. New tests cover Display, Hash, and TzSign.
